hero.kicker: For managing directors and plant managers in manufacturing SMEs
hero.title: Your decision has been made. Why is so little changing in operations?
hero.intro:
The reason is rarely a lack of will. It lies in unclear leadership, unresolved responsibilities and missing alignment at the critical points. That is exactly where I step in.

I work with leadership and directly on the shopfloor in manufacturing companies. Not on concepts, but in leadership situations, coordination and day-to-day operations.

pillars.title: What distinguishes my work
pillars.subtitle: Execution, leadership and sustainable integration in practice

items.title: Execution instead of conceptual overload
items.text: Change is not planned on top of everything else, but made effective within operations. With clear structure, clarified responsibilities and without adding new complexity.

items.title: Clarity in responsibility and alignment
items.text: I do not work with additional programs alongside the organization, but within ongoing operations. Where decisions are made, responsibility is taken and results emerge.

items.title: Experience from shop floor, leadership and management
items.text: My perspective is grounded in direct responsibility in operational and leadership roles within industrial environments. Grown from accountability on the floor, sharpened in parallel through study and research.

home.externalReason: Internal knowledge is rarely the problem. What is missing is an assessment without organisational self-interest. Someone who names what everyone senses but no one internally can say without consequences.

divider.title:

divider.text: You get the combination of my expertise from different angles: hands-on operational responsibility in manufacturing, academic depth on M&A, cultural integration and organisational development, and the ability to work in five languages directly with leadership and workforce.

approach.title: Approach
approach.intro:
Change rarely fails due to missing concepts. It fails because decisions aren't owned, prioritized, or consistently executed.

This is exactly where I step in — at the intersection of leadership, prioritization and execution in ongoing operations.
principles: I work within ongoing operations: Together with leadership, we design clear roles as well as decision-making and steering rhythms, enabling responsibility to be effectively assumed.
I make impact measurable: Together, we define relevant metrics, standards, and routines and embed their follow-up through leadership and decision-making routines.
I anchor change sustainably: We integrate new ways of working into routines, collaboration, as well as culture and identity.

how.title: From trigger to execution — in three steps.
how.subtitle: Not as a concept, but so it works in the day-to-day: clarify together, lead in daily operations, embed consistently.
how.restriction: This approach is not right for every situation. It makes sense when it is already clear that change is necessary, but not taking hold.

steps.text: We understand the current situation, constraints and dynamics—and make the first robust decisions on target state and priorities.
We design and accompany the establishment of a leadership and steering rhythm that reliably enables clarity, prioritization, and execution.
out: Meetings become shorter and more binding

steps.text: We secure impact through follow-up, accountability and cultural fit—until it runs without external support.
out: Change is part of everyday work

about.title: About me
about.heroTitle: I know the operation, the leadership and the pressure behind it.
intro:
I know these situations not from workshops, but from responsibility.
From production and leadership. From phases where decisions had to be made under pressure.

Today I work with leaders and organizations in industrial SMEs at exactly these points.
Where change has been decided but isn't taking hold.
Where efficiency, leadership and organizational culture need to come together.
about.profileText:
Acceptance emerges where language, reality, and responsibility align.

In M&A, integration, and transformation situations, implementation rarely fails due to formal targets, but rather because of hidden cultural and identity-related tensions. My multilingual access to organizations and academic engagement with these dynamics make it possible to identify such tensions early, before they translate into operational or political consequences.

My work is grounded in firsthand experience across shop floor, leadership, and management roles within industrial environments. This leads to a clear approach: change must fit operational reality, be taken up by leadership, and be embedded in everyday work.

This is how implementation emerges — not as something that needs to be explained, but as something that is owned and lived.

speaking.title: Talks & Teaching
speaking.intro:
Talks and teaching formats are not a substitute for the actual work. They serve to make connections visible and open up discussions.

I speak about leadership, change and operational reality. Not from a theoretical distance, but from responsibility within the organization.

topics.title: Efficiency and Culture in Balance
topics.subtitle: Why transformations fail — and what makes them work
topics.description: Transformation is never purely technical; it is always cultural as well. When strategies fail in everyday reality, it is often the tension between efficiency pressure and loss of identity. This talk shows how to connect both perspectives so change is not only designed, but understood and carried in daily operations.

topics.title: Shopfloor Leadership
topics.subtitle: Leading through rhythm, not firefighting
topics.description: Impact is created where value is produced. When shopfloor leadership is replaced by constant firefighting, stability is lost. I show how clear routines, meaningful metrics, and a reliable leadership cadence create orientation — and make accountability effective where problems actually arise.

topics.title: Lean Management
topics.subtitle: Daily impact instead of a toolbox obsession
topics.description: Lean is not a toolbox; it is a logic of simplification and learning. Many initiatives fail not because methods are missing, but because they do not fit daily reality. This impulse focuses on a few levers that stabilize standards, problem solving, and collaboration — without ‘method hunting’.

topics.title: M&A Integration
topics.subtitle: Culture, identity, and the operating model before and after the deal
topics.description: The economic success of mergers is decided after closing — in collaboration, leadership, and identity. Drawing on practice and DBA research, I highlight how culture and identity can be addressed early and how an operating model can be shaped to protect performance without destroying the cultural DNA that made the business successful.

topics.title: Change Governance
topics.subtitle: Decide, communicate, embed
topics.description: Change needs a clear frame; otherwise ambiguity and friction take over. Change governance is the operating system of transformation: decision paths, roles, cadence, and communication. This talk shows how to build governance pragmatically so decisions stick, communication builds trust, and new ways of working don’t fade out.

topics.title: Leadership in Transition
topics.subtitle: Role, impact, accountability
topics.description: In transformation phases, expectations on leaders shift markedly: from subject-matter expert to a builder of orientation, accountability, and collaboration. I reflect on how leadership stays effective under uncertainty, how roles are clarified, and how accountability is placed where it truly matters in daily operations.
